purpose: Identify the named Stage33-05 J2 class inside the four exact resolved-contact pairing orbits without identifying those orbit bits with the fixed marked transcendental Brauer bits.

source_lock.semantic_theorem: For E self-dual via Pic^0(E)=E, the Kummer character of a two-torsion line bundle T on an E[2] cycle D is the Weil pairing e_2(T,D); bit 1 denotes the nontrivial value -1. This is the standard Weil/Kummer duality, used here only after the contact cycles are materialized exactly.

normalization_elliptic_model.named_cv_class_source: Stage33-05 quotient basis [J2,q1], with J2 represented by f2=(t+(1+sqrt(2)))/(t-(1-sqrt(2))) in the Jacobian quotient.

exact_contact_cycle_torsion.interpretation: The two batch-1 orbit parities are precisely the two sheet-holonomy characters around the resolved left and right contact cycles. Component sheet relabeling changes local endpoint labels but not these cycle parities.

weil_pairing_evaluation.convention: orbit bit is 0 for e2=+1 and 1 for e2=-1
facts: e2 is alternating and nondegenerate on E[2]
for E[2]~=(F2)^2, two distinct nonzero two-torsion points pair to -1

complete_four_class_regression.reason: The two contact cycles D_L=J1+J2 and D_R=J2 are independent in E[2], so their Weil characters separate all four Jacobian two-torsion classes.

exact_conclusion: The named CV J2 special-Brauer/admissible-cover datum selects exactly the resolved-contact pairing orbit (L,R)=(1,0). This closes the batch-2 named-orbit selection problem. It does not identify (L,R) with the fixed marked Brauer basis beta1,beta2 and therefore does not yet select [1,0], [0,1], or [1,1] in Hom(T(Kc),Z/2).
